title: Setting the Appetite
briefing: As Risk Manager you own the risk framework for operations. The CEO, Elena Marsh, wants the board to approve a refreshed risk appetite statement next quarter. The current one is a page of adjectives: 'low', 'moderate', 'zero tolerance'.
Draft measures that people can actually manage to.

context.text: After the ransomware outbreak, the board wants cyber in the appetite statement with real numbers.
MFA coverage and patch age, the KRIs from your cyber work, are ready to use as appetite measures.

evidence.title: Current appetite statement
evidence.body: 'Valtren has zero tolerance for food safety breaches, a low appetite for regulatory breaches, a moderate appetite for operational disruption, and is open to strategic risk in pursuit of growth.'

evidence.title: Available measures
evidence.body: Temperature excursions per 10,000 deliveries (last year 3.1). Regulatory findings per year (2). On-time delivery (93-96%). Unplanned downtime of critical systems (hours per quarter). Revenue from new services (8% of total).

evidence.title: Strategy summary
evidence.body: Grow pharmaceutical cold chain from 8% to 25% of revenue in three years. Pharma clients audit suppliers and expect documented temperature control.

questions.prompt: How should 'zero tolerance for food safety breaches' be expressed so it can be monitored?

options.label: Excursions reaching customers: 0 tolerated without root-cause review; in-transit excursions caught before delivery below 2 per 10,000 deliveries, amber at 2, red at 3
options.feedback: Keeps zero where it's achievable (reaching customers) and sets a measurable limit on the precursor.

options.label: Zero excursions of any kind
options.feedback: Unachievable: it will be breached constantly and then ignored.

options.label: Keep 'zero tolerance': the words matter more than numbers
options.feedback: Words without measures can't be monitored.

questions.prompt: How does the pharma growth strategy change the appetite?

options.label: Appetite for temperature and documentation failures must tighten for pharma lanes, while appetite for investment risk in new capability can be higher
options.feedback: Appetite should enable the strategy: open to building capability, strict on what pharma clients audit.

options.label: No change: appetite is independent of strategy
Become 'open' to all risks to support growth
options.feedback: Growth into regulated pharma needs tighter, not looser, control appetite.

questions.prompt: Which measures belong in the board-level appetite statement?

options.label: Headcount in the risk team
options.feedback: An input, not a measure of risk taken.

options.label: Emails sent to staff about risk

questions.prompt: How do you get the executive team behind the draft?

options.label: Test each measure with its owner (thresholds they can live with and evidence they can produce), then take one agreed draft to the executive
options.feedback: Owners who shaped the limits will manage to them.

options.label: Send it straight to the board for approval
options.feedback: Owners will not manage to limits they never agreed.

options.label: Ask a consultancy to write it

questions.prompt: Once approved, what makes the appetite real day to day?

options.label: Cascade each board measure into business-unit limits and KRIs, with breach reporting through the committee
options.feedback: Board appetite only works when it reaches the people making daily decisions.

options.label: Review it annually at the board
options.feedback: Necessary, but not enough on its own.

lesson: Appetite must be measurable, owned and linked to strategy: tight on what clients and regulators care about, open where the strategy needs to take risk.
